BUG: A deterministically-poison intake (e.g. invalid JSON) is retried on every process_queue run forever with no attempt counting or quarantine; the batch never advances past it and each run burns a dispatch evaluation
MINIMAL_FIX: Add a bounded poison policy in one place: count consecutive failures per intake fingerprint (sidecar file or central_state entry) and after N failures move the file to intakes/quarantine/ with a reason marker instead of leaving it pending; surface the quarantine in courier_status output. Pin with a test: invalid-JSON intake is quarantined after the bound and later runs skip it.
RAW_EVIDENCE: scripts/queue_processor.py process_queue(): per-file try/except prints and continues (good: no batch abort), but the poison file stays in intakes/pending with no counter, no quarantine dir, no marker; dispatch_intake fails closed via sys.exit(1) which the caller swallows as retryable. Probe /tmp/probe_p6_quarantine.py: 3 consecutive process_queue runs re-attempt the same invalid-JSON file, pending stays 1, quarantine 0 -> NO_QUARANTINE=True. Contrast docs/META_DISPATCH_AND_RETRY_POLICY.md DO_NOT_RETRY ('identical state repeats beyond limit') and the fingerprint idempotency already in intake_dispatcher.py (which solved re-dispatch but not poison parking).
REPRO_STEPS: 1. In an isolated cwd, create intakes/pending/poison.json with invalid JSON. 2. Run process_queue() three times. 3. File remains in pending, nothing in processed or quarantine, same error each run. See /tmp/probe_p6_quarantine.py.
TARGETED_TEST: Place an invalid-JSON intake in pending, run process_queue past the failure bound, and assert the file lands in intakes/quarantine/ and subsequent runs do not re-attempt it.
